evals.name: reverse-engineer-taskboard
evals.prompt: I have an internal app called taskboard (Express + TypeScript + Postgres). I want you to go through the codebase and create a set of spec documents that will be the source of truth for the application — docs that an AI agent (or a new engineer) can read to know exactly how things should be done in this codebase. Put them under docs/ in the project. The codebase is at the current working directory. I'm not available to answer questions, so make reasonable calls and flag anything I should confirm.
evals.expected_output: A docs/ directory with 00-index.md, numbered topic specs (architecture, data model, API conventions, etc.), docs/decisions/ ADRs, conflict detection (error shape, casing, pagination, README port) surfaced rather than silently averaged, and an AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pointer.
assertions: docs/00-index.md exists and contains a document-index table listing every spec file with a one-line description
Spec files are numbered NN-kebab-topic.md with no gaps or duplicate numbers
A docs/decisions/ directory exists with a README (template + when-to-write guidance) and at least 2 ADRs following the Status/Date/Context/Decision/Alternatives/Consequences structure
The error-shape conflict (boards.ts bare {error} vs tasks.ts {code,message}) is explicitly surfaced as a conflict with one canonical rule chosen, not silently averaged or documented as both-are-fine
The field-casing conflict (camelCase in boards.ts vs snake_case in tasks.ts) is explicitly surfaced with a canonical rule
The pagination conflict (offset in users.ts vs cursor in tasks.ts) is explicitly surfaced with a canonical rule
The README-vs-code port discrepancy (8080 vs 3000) is flagged somewhere in the docs
Flagged assumptions/conflicts are collected in a reviewable place (e.g. an 'Assumed conventions — confirm these' section in the index)
Specs make only claims that are true of the fixture code (no invented endpoints, tables, or infrastructure)
An agent-instructions pointer exists (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md telling agents to read docs/00-index.md first and treat specs as source of truth)
Normative rules are written in the imperative with reasons, not vague descriptions ('errors are generally JSON')

evals.name: greenfield-recipe-planner
evals.prompt: I'm about to start building a new app and want spec docs in place first so my coding agents follow them. The app: 'mealprep' — a web app where a family plans weekly dinners, keeps a shared recipe library, and auto-generates a grocery list from the week's plan. Decisions I've already made: Next.js (app router) + TypeScript, Postgres via Prisma, deployed on Vercel, auth via Clerk, single household per account for v1 (sharing across households is later). REST API routes under /api. I want cursor pagination and a consistent JSON error shape, you pick the details. Create the spec document set in ./docs as the source of truth. I won't be around to answer follow-ups, so use the details above and mark assumptions.
evals.expected_output: A docs/ set for a greenfield app: index with doc map and key-decisions table, scope spec with explicit v1 boundary (multi-household marked post-v1), architecture, data model, API conventions with concrete error/pagination rules, ADRs for the stated decisions (Next.js, Prisma, Clerk, Vercel), assumptions marked.
assertions: docs/00-index.md exists with a document-index table, a product summary, and a key-decisions table
Spec files are numbered NN-kebab-topic.md with no gaps or duplicate numbers
A scope spec exists with an explicit v1 boundary and multi-household sharing marked as post-v1/deferred
docs/decisions/ contains a README and ADRs covering the user's stated decisions (at least 3 of: Next.js, Prisma/Postgres, Clerk, Vercel)
API conventions spec defines a concrete error shape (named fields, HTTP status mapping) and concrete cursor-pagination request/response shapes — not just 'we use cursor pagination'
A data-model spec exists covering households, recipes, meal plans, and grocery lists with relationships
Assumptions the agent made beyond the prompt are explicitly marked as assumptions
Specs cross-reference each other and ADRs with working relative links
An agent-instructions pointer exists (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md directing agents to docs/00-index.md as source of truth)
Each spec opens with a TL;DR blockquote immediately after the title
